summary.headline: Eicher Motors Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 32% to INR 6,632 crore with record Royal Enfield volumes of 332,940 units.
summary.overview: Eicher Motors posted its best-ever Q1 with consolidated revenue of INR 6,632 crore (up 32% YoY), EBITDA of INR 1,591 crore and PAT of INR 1,463 crore (up 21%). Royal Enfield sold a record 332,940 motorcycles (up from 261,326), and VECV recorded its highest-ever Q1 sales of 24,815 units (up 14.8%). Management flagged a tight dealer inventory of 10-12 days ahead of festive season, with capacity ramp-up at Cheyyar and a greenfield Tada (Andhra Pradesh) plant approved. Commodity inflation of 4-4.5% of costs was partly offset by price hikes and value engineering, and softening was noted.

1.2% price hikes, 1% international mix, 0.4% currency, 0.6% allied business; offset by lower value

financial_highlights.value: Above INR 1,000 crore, about 15.3% of revenue

financial_highlights.change: INR 30 crore timing (Q4 ad campaign and launches) plus INR 22 crore marketing control

segments.name: Royal Enfield (India)
segments.commentary: 301,174 motorcycles sold in India; management cites about 32% volume growth and 350cc models (Classic, Bullet, Hunter, Meteor) up about 34% YoY. 450cc and 650cc models are back to pre-GST price levels, with Guerrilla 450 at about 2,400-2,500 units per month and 650cc twins at about 4,000-4,200 per month.

segments.name: Royal Enfield (International)
segments.commentary: Global volume 31,766 motorcycles; Brazil is the largest overseas market (about every fourth exported motorcycle), with a planned CKD facility. Europe remains in a market adjustment phase; US shows early green shoots after a tariff cut.

segments.name: Flying Flea (EV)
segments.commentary: Flying Flea C6 launched and deliveries started this quarter; about 100+ units delivered in two months, with Bengaluru expansion to 10 touchpoints and about 6 further cities planned.

segments.name: VECV (commercial vehicles)
segments.commentary: Total 24,815 units (up 14.8%); Eicher heavy-duty 5,275 units (up 15.2%, 8.8% share); light and medium-duty 9,993 units; Eicher buses 6,126 units; Volvo trucks and buses record 598 units; exports 1,450 units (up 14.7%); spares sales INR 931.3 crore (up 15.3%).

segments.name: Allied / aftermarket
segments.commentary: Allied businesses about 15% of revenue; about 9 lakh service job cards per month (up about 20% YoY); accessories and apparel growing above 30%, with accessory attach rate at about 87% per management.

guidance_outlook: Management expects growth momentum to continue; no formal numerical guidance given. Commodity outlook not quantified because the situation is described as volatile.
Royal Enfield Cheyyar brownfield (INR 958 crore announced in Feb 2026) expected to reach 2 million units per year capacity by FY28.
Tada greenfield Phase 1 (INR 1,225 crore, approved today) adds about 4.5 lakh units per year at full utilisation, with completion expected in FY30; total capacity to reach 2.45 million units by FY30.
Next Cheyyar module expected to kick in by first week of October 2026.
Indonesia CKD decision expected within the current quarter.
capex_capacity: Current Royal Enfield build capacity about 1.5 million motorcycles per year after first Cheyyar module, which started in July 2026 (in time); delivery rate reached about 5,000+ per day.
June 2026 production about 1.16 lakh motorcycles, with about 4,500 per day rate; Oragadam and Vallam running three shifts since April.
Tada greenfield in Andhra Pradesh: INR 1,225 crore Phase 1, additional 4.5 lakh units per year at full utilisation, built in modules.
Depreciation rise attributed to about INR 346 crore increase in average gross block, mainly Flying Flea start of production and new capacity, plus tools and dies depreciation.
Indonesia: CKD assembly partner identified to get around 10,000-unit annual import quota limit; luxury tax about 160%+ applies to bikes above 250cc regardless of CBU/CKD.
demand_pricing: Royal Enfield India retail growth about 30-32% YoY in Q1; booking, walk-in and telephonic inquiries growing slightly faster than volumes.

Dealer inventory at about 10-12 days, described as lean; in-transit inventory about 5 days and depot inventory about 4-5 days additional, per Q&A. Management targets saving another 4-5 days via more direct billing (about 4.5-4.7x increase vs prior year).
Gross margin: commodity and input inflation net impact about 4-4.5% of costs in Q1; value engineering benefit about 0.4%; 350cc price hike of 1.75% from April 2026 gave about 1.2% benefit.
Hunter 350 first-time buyers about 50% share; overall RE customer mix about 70%+ upgraders, about 25% first-time buyers, about 5-6% repeat RE-to-RE.
VECV: spares growth 15.3%; Pro X SCV entry with 1,041 units including 172 EVs; PARIVARTAN fleet modernisation MoU for NCR targets over 2 lakh vehicles, implementation being finalised.

qa_highlights.question: Where is the brownfield capacity ramp and what is channel inventory ahead of festive?
qa_highlights.answer: First module started July 2026, output about 5,000+ per day delivery; inventory about 10-12 days, lean; direct billing and vendor 3-shift planning aimed to build stock before festive; next module by October first week.

qa_highlights.question: What is the gross margin bridge and the drivers of lower other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Net commodity/input impact about 4-4.5%, value engineering about 0.4%, price hikes about 1.2%, mix 0.2%. Other expenses down about 7%: INR 30 crore from Q4 timing (cricket ads, two launches) and INR 22 crore marketing cut. No forward commodity guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: What is demand outlook into the back half given high base from October?
qa_highlights.answer: Management points to strong funnel growth, a middleweight segment that grew from 70,000 to 1.2 lakh units per month in three years, planned launches, and a marketing ramp-up after scaling back in Q1 FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue gap between standalone and consolidated and its sustainability?
qa_highlights.answer: Gap driven by subsidiary growth, mainly Brazil, with some offset from India-booked exports; international market size about 0.8-1 million units, Royal Enfield share 8-9%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is ASP up and what is driving non-vehicle revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: ASP up 2.8% QoQ: price hikes 1.2%, international mix 1%, currency 0.4%, allied 0.6%. Allied about 15% of revenue, service job cards about 9 lakh per month.

qa_highlights.question: Any plans to list or hive off VECV?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no crystallised plan; focus at Eicher level is on EV; VECV growth described as phenomenal across segments except heavy-duty buses.

risks_watch: Inventory tightness at about 10-12 days ahead of festive; ability of vendors to sustain 24/7 three-shift output and the October module timing.
Commodity inflation (aluminium, crude, steel, copper, precious metals) and logistics disruption; management declined to guide on Q2 commodity headwind.
Higher-cc (450cc/650cc) softness in Super Meteor, Himalayan and Shotgun in Q1 per analyst; management plans marketing and refreshes.
High base from October for the next 12 months after GST-related price cuts.
Europe and APAC still weak; Indonesia import quota and luxury tax constrain ASEAN growth; Flying Flea scale-up and EV economics still early.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on volumes and demand, describing Q1 as exceptional for both businesses; more measured on commodity costs, which management called volatile and declined to quantify forward. Evasive on VECV listing, saying no crystallised plan exists.
key_quotes: There has been an exceptional quarter across both the businesses.
Currently, we are at a very low inventory.
We are cautiously bullish even in the international market.
So we are taking it in phases because the growth momentum is continuing.

growth.why: No formal numerical revenue guidance; management says growth momentum will continue, backed by first Cheyyar module live since July 2026 (about 1.5M units/yr build capacity), next module by early October, and Tada Phase 1 (INR 1,225 cr, approved) targeting 2.45M total capacity by FY30, with Q1 revenue up 32% and RE volumes up about 27%.
